newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian cocoa bean exports down in April.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian cocoa bean exports down in April.

text.p: Cocoa bean exports from Ivory Coast fell to 116,598 tonnes in April, against 171,104 tonnes in March, and 121,187 in April last year, according to official shipping data.
Abidjan handled 67,604 tonnes of April 1997 exports, with a further 48,994 tonnes leaving via the second Ivorian port of San Pedro, the data show.
Cumulative exports for the first seven months of 1996/97 (Oct-Sept) totalled 883,935 tonnes, against 843,833 by the end of April in 1995/96.

The main destinations for April exports from Abidjan were north west European ports, which took 43,560 tonnes, including 31,590 for Amsterdam. U.S. east coast ports took 6,257 tonnes, including 2,867 for New York.
Separate figures by destination for San Pedro were not immediately available.
Ivory Coast produced a record crop of 1.2 million tonnes of cocoa in 1995/96 and private forecasts for the total 1996/97 crop range up to around 1.15 million tonnes.
